6	> # Tabula: seven more commands
7	>
8	> This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
9	> library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
10	> `head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
11	> all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
12	> returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
13	> statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
14	> command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.
15	>
16	> How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
17	> default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
18	> `tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
19	> right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
20	> data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
21	> text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
22	> thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
23	> does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).
24	>
25	> Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
26	> command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
27	> usage error (exit 2).
28	>
29	> ## sort
30	>
31	> `tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
32	> name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
33	> either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
34	> stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
35	> number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
36	> error. At least one KEY is needed.
37	>
38	> ## filter
39	>
40	> `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
41	> is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
42	> are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
43	> the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
44	> same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
45	> they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
46	> argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
47	> table with no row left still prints its header.
48	>
49	> ## group
50	>
51	> `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
52	> appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
53	> AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
54	> that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
55	> `mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
56	> `2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
57	> message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
58	> usage error.
59	>
60	> ## join
61	>
62	> `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
63	> LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
64	> If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
65	> the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
66	> row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
67	> with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.
68	>
69	> ## pivot
70	>
71	> `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
72	> ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
73	> the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
74	> COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
75	> error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
76	> COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
77	> a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.
78	>
79	> ## dedupe
80	>
81	> `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
82	> With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
83	> rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.
84	>
85	> ## stats
86	>
87	> `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
88	> `max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
89	> whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
90	> are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
91	> with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
92	> row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.

> `tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
> right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
> data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
> text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
> thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
> does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).
>
> Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
> command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
> usage error (exit 2).
>
> ## sort
>
> `tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
> name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
> either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
> stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
> number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
> error. At least one KEY is needed.
>
> ## filter
>
> `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
> is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
> are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
> the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
> same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
> they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
> argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
> table with no row left still prints its header.
>
> ## group
>
> `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
> appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
> AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
> that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
> `mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
> `2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
> message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
> usage error.
>
> ## join
>
> `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
> LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
> If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
> the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
> row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
> with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.
>
> ## pivot
>
> `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
> ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
> the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
> COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
> error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
> COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
> a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.
>
> ## dedupe
>
> `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
> With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
> rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.
>
> ## stats
>
> `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
> `max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
> whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
> are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
> with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
> row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.
>

LONG WAITS (#1042, #1066) — never wait inside your session; the engine waits for you. Your prompt cache lives 5 minutes: a foreground `sleep` loop that wakes after 9-10 minutes rewrites your whole context as a cache write (150K-300K tokens, about $1 per wake on Sonnet, against about $0.08 for a cache read), and that pattern was 72% of three days' spend. A job that may run longer than about 4 minutes (a suite, a gate, a bench batch, a Windows-host run, a build): start it with `harness-wait run --deadline-s <most seconds it may take> --log <logfile> -- <command…>`, then END YOUR TURN at once: one short reply naming what you wait for (no promise, no more tool calls). `harness-wait run` starts the command detached, keeps its output in the log and its exit code in `<logfile>.rc`, and writes your wait spec; the engine checks it for you at no model cost and resumes this session ONCE, when the job exits or the deadline passes, with `wait done: <condition>, rc=<n>, log tail: …`. Judge the result from that message and read the log for more; never loop on it. Other conditions: `harness-wait set --deadline-s <s> --pid <pid>` (a process exits), `--path <file>` (a file appears), `--regex <re> --log <file>` (a line appears in a log from now on). Not allowed, whatever the Bash timeout: `for i in $(seq 1 58); do …; sleep 10; done`, `timeout 585 bash -c "until …"`, `end=$((SECONDS+570)); while …`, or a Bash `run_in_background` you then keep polling. A wait on another lane (a lock queue, a merge, a PR) is not a job you can run: park the lane where a park exists (a lock queue, #1034) instead of polling. A usage limit needs nothing from you: the engine parks the lane and resumes it once the limit has cleared. If you park yourself on a limit or a reset time (`harness-wait set --limit --until <epoch>`), omit `--deadline-s`: the deadline resumes you too, and `waitlib` refuses one that ends before `--until` (#1100). A wait that ends HOURS from now (more than 2 hours: a bench or budget block waiting for a usage window to reset, `harness-wait set --limit --until <epoch>`, or `--path <file> --deadline-s <s>`) PARKS you (#1154): commit and push first, then run it; it posts your handoff, swaps `agent-working` for the `waiting-quota` label and ends your session, so your pool slot goes to the next ready issue, and the engine re-dispatches the issue as a resume once the wait is over — do nothing more after it prints `PARKED`. A refusal (unpushed work) leaves your session as it was; `--resume inject` keeps your slot, and is for waits you really must hold. Never sit on a pool slot for hours. Polling you cannot avoid: one short check per wake, each wake under 270 seconds so the cache stays warm. Never a blocking loop. SUB-AGENTS (#1249) — your own sub-agents are not jobs you can wait on, and each one's notification is a wake after the 5-minute cache expired (140K-350K tokens of cache write each; four bangwa lanes were parked for it). Sub-agents always run in the background here. Start every sub-agent of one fan-out in ONE message, so they start together and tend to finish together. Every sub-agent brief tells it to run every command in the foreground: no `run_in_background`, `Monitor` or `harness-wait run` inside a sub-agent, and never end its turn before its final report. Each sub-agent then notifies you exactly once; one that backgrounds its work and ends its turn sends an interim "completed" you pay a wake for, and a second when it really finishes. When a sub-agent's notification arrives while other sub-agents are still running, make no tool calls: write one short line and end your turn (no re-reading files, no `git status`, no check on the others). Never poll a sub-agent (`TaskOutput`, reading its output file, or `sleep`). SUB-AGENT SCOPE (#1252) — every call re-reads your whole context from cache: on one fleet that was 65% of its spend, with lanes at 695k and sub-agents at 804k tokens and no compaction ever. The engine sets a context budget (`HARNESS_LANE_CONTEXT_MAX`, default 200k) and Claude Code compacts a lane and each of its sub-agents when it reaches it; stay well under it yourself. A sub-agent is ONE bounded task: its brief names the files it reads and edits, the tests it runs and the checkboxes it owns, and nothing more. It never reads the whole repo (no tree-wide `git grep`, `find` or `cat` sweeps, no files outside its brief) and never pastes a whole file, diff or test log into its context: it reads the lines it needs, tails and greps logs. It hands back a SUMMARY of at most 30 lines (what changed, the test result, any defect it did not fix), never file contents. A merge or conflict-resolution sub-agent resolves ONLY the files it is given, one conflicted file or a few that depend on each other, reading those files, their conflict markers and the commit messages of the two sides, and nothing else; the rest of the merge stays with its parent. Work that runs on (about 100 calls) goes to a FRESH sub-agent with a new brief, never to a longer-running one; you keep the summaries, not their transcripts.

PRD: tabula — seven more commands (sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats) [{'id': 'LA_kwDOVy0_hc8AAAADDoS6BQ', 'name': 'prd', 'description': 'PRD tracking issue', 'color': '5319e7'}]
## Problem Statement

`tabula` (Python 3.9+, standard library only) has four commands today: `show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`. Sorting, filtering, grouping, joining, pivoting, deduplicating and summarising a CSV file all have to be done some other way.

## Solution

Add seven commands to `tabula/engine.py`: `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats`. Each one is built the way the first four were: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that returns a `Table`, plus one entry in `COMMANDS`. Each command also gets its own `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (written like the four that are there, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, after `apply`) and an entry in the README's command list. Add two global options, `--kind inner|left` (read by `join`) and `--keep first|last` (read by `dedupe`).

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I can `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers and get a stable sort.
2. As a CSV user, I can `tabula filter FILE COND...` with `== != >= <= > < ~` and keep only the rows that match.
3. As a CSV user, I can `tabula group FILE BY AGG...` with `count`, `sum:`, `min:`, `max:` and `mean:` aggregates.
4. As a CSV user, I can `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` as an inner or a left join.
5. As a CSV user, I can `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` to sum VALUE into a ROW × COLUMN grid.
6. As a CSV user, I can `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` and keep the first or the last row of each duplicate set.
7. As a CSV user, I can `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` to get count/min/max/mean/median for each column.
8. As an existing user, the four existing commands, their output and their exit statuses do not change. `pip install .` still gives the `tabula` command and `import tabula`.

## Implementation Decisions

- Everything goes into `tabula/engine.py`. No new modules for commands.
- **Finish the module's conventions before adding to them, and do not add a second way to do something it already does.** In practice:
  - **Option reading:** `parse_args` hard-codes `--format`. Turn it into one table-driven reader (option name → allowed values, default) that handles `--format`, `--kind` and `--keep` the same way: `--opt value` or `--opt=value`, before or after the command, accepted on any command line. An unknown value, a missing value or an unknown option exits 2. Defaults: format=text, kind=inner, keep=first. Existing `--format` messages and behaviour stay the same.
  - **Numbers:** reuse `to_decimal` / `fmt_decimal` / `NUMBER`. Add one shared helper for "this cell must be a number" that raises `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number`. sort, group, pivot and stats all use it. Add one shared helper for "round half up to 2 decimals and always print two" (used by group's mean and by stats' mean/median). Plain-number output (sum/min/max) goes through `fmt_decimal`, which already prints no exponent and keeps `10.50` as `10.50`. `Decimal` everywhere, never float.
  - **Usage errors** go through `_need_args` / `UsageError`, in the same style as the existing commands ("usage: tabula sort FILE KEY..."). Missing columns go through `Table.index` (exit 1, the message names the column).
  - "row N" counts the data rows from 1 in file order (the header is not counted), never in sorted order.
- **Decomposition / ordering:** seven child issues, one per command. Each can be built, tested and merged on its own. The `sort` issue lands the shared groundwork above (option table incl. `--kind`/`--keep`, the numeric-cell helper, the 2-dp helper). The other six are `## Blocked by` the sort issue, so they build on the finished conventions and do not each invent their own. After that the six are independent. They all touch `COMMANDS`, `docs/commands.md` and the README list, so expect to rebase on each other.
- Behaviour for each command is exactly as in the Original request below (it is the spec). Decisions made where the brief leaves room:
  - sort: an unknown modifier (e.g. `price:foo`) or an empty column name is a usage error (exit 2), and so is a repeated modifier.
  - filter: VALUE may be empty (`city==` matches empty cells). For numeric comparison, both the cell and VALUE must pass `to_decimal`.
  - group: aggregate column names replace every `:` with `_`. A column named in `sum:X` that does not exist → exit 1. `sum:` with no column → usage error.
  - join: duplicate column names after the `_right` renaming → exit 1, naming the column.
  - pivot: the exit-1 checks (empty COLUMN value, COLUMN value equal to the ROW column name, non-number VALUE) report the first offending row in file order.
  - stats: `min`/`max` print as in `group`.

## Testing Decisions

- One test file per command, `tests/test_NAME.py`, using `unittest`, in the style of `tests/test_engine.py` (call `main([...])` and capture stdout/stderr and the exit status). Cover the happy path in all three `--format`s where it matters, each mistake (exit 1, the exact message, nothing on stdout) and each usage error (exit 2).
- The option-reader changes are tested in the sort issue's test file: `--kind`/`--keep` before and after the command, the `=` form, and a bad value → 2.
- `python -m unittest discover tests` must stay green, including the existing `tests/test_engine.py`.

## Out of Scope

- New transforms, new output formats, or changes to how the existing four commands behave.
- Third-party dependencies, and any floating-point arithmetic.
- Commands other than these seven.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_args` reads options from one table. `--format`, `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last` are accepted on any command, before or after it, as `--opt v` or `--opt=v`. A bad value exits 2.
- [ ] One shared numeric-cell helper produces `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number`. One shared 2-dp half-up helper. No duplicated number parsing.
- [ ] `sort` behaves as specified: multi-key, `:num`/`:desc` in either order, stable incl. desc, code-point text order, repeated modifier → 2, no KEY → 2. Has `tests/test_sort.py`.
- [ ] `filter` behaves as specified: the first operator wins and the longer one at the same position, numeric vs text comparison, case-insensitive `~`, header kept with zero rows, no operator / empty column → 2. Has `tests/test_filter.py`.
- [ ] `group` behaves as specified: first-appearance order, `count/sum/min/max/mean` naming with `_`, mean always 2 dp half up, bad or duplicate aggregate → 2, no aggregate → 2. Has `tests/test_group.py`.
- [ ] `join` behaves as specified: inner (default) / left, `_right` renaming, a remaining duplicate name → 1, exactly 3 args. Has `tests/test_join.py`.
- [ ] `pivot` behaves as specified: first-appearance order of rows and columns, sums printed as in group, missing pair `0`, ROW==COLUMN → 2, empty COLUMN value → 1, COLUMN value equal to the ROW name → 1, exactly 4 args. Has `tests/test_pivot.py`.
- [ ] `dedupe` behaves as specified: `--keep first` (default) / `last`, survivors in file order, at least one KEY. Has `tests/test_dedupe.py`.
- [ ] `stats` behaves as specified: columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, whitespace-only cells skipped, exact median, an all-empty column → `COLUMN,0,,,,`. Has `tests/test_stats.py`.
- [ ] `docs/commands.md` has one section per new command, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats. The README command list names all eleven.
- [ ] The existing four commands, their output and their exit statuses are unchanged. `pip install .` gives `tabula` and `import tabula`. The full suite passes.

## Original request

> # Tabula: seven more commands
>
> This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
> library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
> `head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
> all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
> returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
> statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
> command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.
>
> How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
> default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
> `tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
> right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
> data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
> text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
> thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
> does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).
>
> Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
> command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
> usage error (exit 2).
>
> ## sort
>
> `tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
> name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
> either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
> stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
> number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
> error. At least one KEY is needed.
>
> ## filter
>
> `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
> is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
> are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
> the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
> same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
> they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
> argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
> table with no row left still prints its header.
>
> ## group
>
> `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
> appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
> AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
> that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
> `mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
> `2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
> message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
> usage error.
>
> ## join
>
> `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
> LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
> If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
> the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
> row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
> with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.
>
> ## pivot
>
> `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
> ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
> the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
> COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
> error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
> COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
> a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.
>
> ## dedupe
>

## Problem Statement

`tabula` (Python 3.9+, standard library only) has four commands today: `show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`. Sorting, filtering, grouping, joining, pivoting, deduplicating and summarising a CSV file all have to be done some other way.

## Solution

Add seven commands to `tabula/engine.py`: `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats`. Each one is built the way the first four were: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that returns a `Table`, plus one entry in `COMMANDS`. Each command also gets its own `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (written like the four that are there, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, after `apply`) and an entry in the README's command list. Add two global options, `--kind inner|left` (read by `join`) and `--keep first|last` (read by `dedupe`).

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I can `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers and get a stable sort.
2. As a CSV user, I can `tabula filter FILE COND...` with `== != >= <= > < ~` and keep only the rows that match.
3. As a CSV user, I can `tabula group FILE BY AGG...` with `count`, `sum:`, `min:`, `max:` and `mean:` aggregates.
4. As a CSV user, I can `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` as an inner or a left join.
5. As a CSV user, I can `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` to sum VALUE into a ROW × COLUMN grid.
6. As a CSV user, I can `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` and keep the first or the last row of each duplicate set.
7. As a CSV user, I can `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` to get count/min/max/mean/median for each column.
8. As an existing user, the four existing commands, their output and their exit statuses do not change. `pip install .` still gives the `tabula` command and `import tabula`.

## Implementation Decisions

- Everything goes into `tabula/engine.py`. No new modules for commands.
- **Finish the module's conventions before adding to them, and do not add a second way to do something it already does.** In practice:
  - **Option reading:** `parse_args` hard-codes `--format`. Turn it into one table-driven reader (option name → allowed values, default) that handles `--format`, `--kind` and `--keep` the same way: `--opt value` or `--opt=value`, before or after the command, accepted on any command line. An unknown value, a missing value or an unknown option exits 2. Defaults: format=text, kind=inner, keep=first. Existing `--format` messages and behaviour stay the same.
  - **Numbers:** reuse `to_decimal` / `fmt_decimal` / `NUMBER`. Add one shared helper for "this cell must be a number" that raises `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number`. sort, group, pivot and stats all use it. Add one shared helper for "round half up to 2 decimals and always print two" (used by group's mean and by stats' mean/median). Plain-number output (sum/min/max) goes through `fmt_decimal`, which already prints no exponent and keeps `10.50` as `10.50`. `Decimal` everywhere, never float.
  - **Usage errors** go through `_need_args` / `UsageError`, in the same style as the existing commands ("usage: tabula sort FILE KEY..."). Missing columns go through `Table.index` (exit 1, the message names the column).
  - "row N" counts the data rows from 1 in file order (the header is not counted), never in sorted order.
- **Decomposition / ordering:** seven child issues, one per command. Each can be built, tested and merged on its own. The `sort` issue lands the shared groundwork above (option table incl. `--kind`/`--keep`, the numeric-cell helper, the 2-dp helper). The other six are `## Blocked by` the sort issue, so they build on the finished conventions and do not each invent their own. After that the six are independent. They all touch `COMMANDS`, `docs/commands.md` and the README list, so expect to rebase on each other.
- Behaviour for each command is exactly as in the Original request below (it is the spec). Decisions made where the brief leaves room:
  - sort: an unknown modifier (e.g. `price:foo`) or an empty column name is a usage error (exit 2), and so is a repeated modifier.
  - filter: VALUE may be empty (`city==` matches empty cells). For numeric comparison, both the cell and VALUE must pass `to_decimal`.
  - group: aggregate column names replace every `:` with `_`. A column named in `sum:X` that does not exist → exit 1. `sum:` with no column → usage error.
  - join: duplicate column names after the `_right` renaming → exit 1, naming the column.
  - pivot: the exit-1 checks (empty COLUMN value, COLUMN value equal to the ROW column name, non-number VALUE) report the first offending row in file order.
  - stats: `min`/`max` print as in `group`.

## Testing Decisions

- One test file per command, `tests/test_NAME.py`, using `unittest`, in the style of `tests/test_engine.py` (call `main([...])` and capture stdout/stderr and the exit status). Cover the happy path in all three `--format`s where it matters, each mistake (exit 1, the exact message, nothing on stdout) and each usage error (exit 2).
- The option-reader changes are tested in the sort issue's test file: `--kind`/`--keep` before and after the command, the `=` form, and a bad value → 2.
- `python -m unittest discover tests` must stay green, including the existing `tests/test_engine.py`.

## Out of Scope

- New transforms, new output formats, or changes to how the existing four commands behave.
- Third-party dependencies, and any floating-point arithmetic.
- Commands other than these seven.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_args` reads options from one table. `--format`, `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last` are accepted on any command, before or after it, as `--opt v` or `--opt=v`. A bad value exits 2.
- [ ] One shared numeric-cell helper produces `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number`. One shared 2-dp half-up helper. No duplicated number parsing.
- [ ] `sort` behaves as specified: multi-key, `:num`/`:desc` in either order, stable incl. desc, code-point text order, repeated modifier → 2, no KEY → 2. Has `tests/test_sort.py`.
- [ ] `filter` behaves as specified: the first operator wins and the longer one at the same position, numeric vs text comparison, case-insensitive `~`, header kept with zero rows, no operator / empty column → 2. Has `tests/test_filter.py`.
- [ ] `group` behaves as specified: first-appearance order, `count/sum/min/max/mean` naming with `_`, mean always 2 dp half up, bad or duplicate aggregate → 2, no aggregate → 2. Has `tests/test_group.py`.
- [ ] `join` behaves as specified: inner (default) / left, `_right` renaming, a remaining duplicate name → 1, exactly 3 args. Has `tests/test_join.py`.
- [ ] `pivot` behaves as specified: first-appearance order of rows and columns, sums printed as in group, missing pair `0`, ROW==COLUMN → 2, empty COLUMN value → 1, COLUMN value equal to the ROW name → 1, exactly 4 args. Has `tests/test_pivot.py`.
- [ ] `dedupe` behaves as specified: `--keep first` (default) / `last`, survivors in file order, at least one KEY. Has `tests/test_dedupe.py`.
- [ ] `stats` behaves as specified: columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`, whitespace-only cells skipped, exact median, an all-empty column → `COLUMN,0,,,,`. Has `tests/test_stats.py`.
- [ ] `docs/commands.md` has one section per new command, in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats. The README command list names all eleven.
- [ ] The existing four commands, their output and their exit statuses are unchanged. `pip install .` gives `tabula` and `import tabula`. The full suite passes.

import io

from decimal import (Context, Decimal, InvalidOperation, MAX_EMAX, MAX_PREC, MIN_EMIN, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR,

NUMBER = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)")

    if number is None:

# --- the table -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Table:
    """Column names and rows of strings. `source` names where it came from, for messages."""

    def __init__(self, columns, rows, source="<table>"):
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.rows = [list(r) for r in rows]
        self.source = source

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.rows)

    def index(self, name):
        """Position of a column; TabulaError when there is none."""
        try:
            return self.columns.index(name)
        except ValueError:
            raise TabulaError("%s: no column %r (columns: %s)" % (self.source, name, ", ".join(self.columns)))

    def column(self, name):
        at = self.index(name)
        return [row[at] for row in self.rows]

    def dicts(self):
        return [dict(zip(self.columns, row)) for row in self.rows]

    def with_rows(self, rows, columns=None):
        return Table(self.columns if columns is None else columns, rows, self.source)


def parse_text(text, source):
    """CSV text into a Table. Blank lines are ignored; every row must have as many fields as the header."""
    if text.startswith("﻿"):
        text = text[1:]
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
    columns, rows = None, []
    try:
        for fields in reader:
            if not fields:
                continue
            if columns is None:
                for name in fields:
                    if not name.strip():
                        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: empty column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                if len(set(fields)) != len(fields):
                    raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: duplicate column name" % (source, reader.line_num))
                columns = fields
                continue
            if len(fields) != len(columns):
                raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: expected %d fields, found %d"
                                  % (source, reader.line_num, len(columns), len(fields)))
            rows.append(fields)
    except csv.Error as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: line %d: %s" % (source, reader.line_num, exc))
    if columns is None:
        raise TabulaError("%s: no header line" % source)
    return Table(columns, rows, source)


def load(path):
    """Read a CSV file (UTF-8, optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) into a Table."""
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise TabulaError("%s: cannot read: %s" % (path, exc.strerror or exc))
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise TabulaError("%s: not valid UTF-8" % path)
    return parse_text(text, path)


# --- output --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def render_text(table):
    cells = [table.columns] + table.rows
    widths = [max(len(row[i]) for row in cells) for i in range(len(table.columns))]
    lines = ["  ".join(cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(row, widths)).rstrip() for row in cells]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def render_csv(table):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(table.columns)
    writer.writerows(table.rows)
    return out.getvalue()


def render_json(table):
    return json.dumps(table.dicts(), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


RENDERERS = {"text": render_text, "csv": render_csv, "json": render_json}


def render(table, fmt="text"):
    return RENDERERS[fmt](table)

def t_upper(value, arg=None):
    """The value in upper case.

    Example: upper applied to '  Héllo, World 42 "x" ' gives '  HÉLLO, WORLD 42 "X" '.

# Commands

`tabula [--format text|csv|json] [--kind inner|left] [--keep first|last] COMMAND ARGS...` reads CSV files (UTF-8, an optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) and prints
a table. Every command returns a `Table`; `--format` says how it is printed (text by default). The options `--kind` (read by `join`) and `--keep` (read by `dedupe`)
are accepted on any command line; each option goes before or after the command, as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`, and any
other value is a usage error. A mistake in a file or in a
request exits 1 with `tabula: <message>` on standard error; a command line that is not shaped right exits 2.

## show

`tabula show FILE` prints the whole table. Blank lines in the file are ignored. A row with more or fewer fields than the
header is a mistake that names the file and the line (`t.csv: line 3: expected 2 fields, found 1`).

## head

`tabula head FILE N` prints the header and the first N rows. N is a whole number (zero is fine); anything else is a usage
error.

## cols

`tabula cols FILE` prints one row per column with two columns, `position` (from 1) and `column`.

## apply

`tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...` runs each TRANSFORM, left to right, over every value of one column and prints the
whole table. A transform is `name` or `name:ARG`; the list is in `docs/transforms.md`. A value a transform cannot take is
a mistake that names the file and the row (`t.csv: row 2: 'abc' is not a number`). Rows count from 1, the header not
counted.

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column name,
optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in either order
(`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point, so `B` sorts before `a`. The sort is stable: rows that
tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a number is a mistake that
names the file, the row and the column (`t.csv: row 3: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`). At least one KEY is needed;
a modifier that is unknown or given twice in one KEY is a usage error.

## filter

`tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION is one
argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators are `==`,
`!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is the first one
that appears in the argument, so a column name cannot contain one; where two start at the same place the longer one wins
(`>=`, not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers they are compared as numbers (`10` is
greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An argument with no operator, or with nothing before
the operator, is a usage error, and so is a missing CONDITION. A table with no row left still prints its header.

## group

`tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first appears,
with the column BY and then one column per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An AGGREGATE is
`count` (the rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN` or `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of that column.
`sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`). `mean` is the exact
sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`, `2.25`). A cell that is not a
number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake, worded as in `sort`. At least one AGGREGATE is needed;
one that is none of those, or the same one twice, is a usage error. A result that would have a column name twice (BY named
`count`, with the aggregate `count`) is a mistake.

## join

`tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of LEFT,
then the columns of RIGHT except KEY; a RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name, and if that
still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed, which is a mistake. Values match when the text is
exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one row per matching
RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row with no match appears
once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.

## pivot

`tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column ROW,
then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears, and one row per distinct value of ROW in the
order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that COLUMN value,
printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (a usage error otherwise).
An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`t.csv: row 2: column 'q': empty value`), and so is a value of COLUMN equal to the
name of the ROW column, because the result would have that column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is a mistake, worded as
in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.

## dedupe

`tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops the rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The rows that
stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.

## stats

`tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`, `max`,
`mean` and `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only whitespace counts as
empty); all of those must be numbers (a mistake, worded as in `sort`, otherwise). `count` is how many there are. `min` and
`max` are printed as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (the
median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the row is `COLUMN`,
`0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.
